To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a procedure has been established to determine equivalent circuit parameters for brushless doubly fed machines.

(1) a coupled-circuit model can be reduced to a single loop equivalent circuit without significant loss of information and (2) a winding factor based method can be developed to obtain equivalent circuit parameters for both rotor circuits.

the equivalent circuit parameters for brushless doubly fed machines can be determined using either the winding factor method or the coupled-circuit method, both of which are accurate and provide good agreement with finite element analysis results and experimental data.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the determination of parameters of a brushless doubly fed generator.
the modeling and parameter determination of the brushless doubly-fed (induction) motor.
the determination of the equivalent circuit parameters of the brushless doubly-fed (induction) machines (BDFIMs) and the development of a model for predicting their steady-state behavior.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the winding factor method is more general and more accurate for the brushless machine.
the method based on winding factor analysis is preferred for its simplicity.
the method presented here is the most accurate, and the method presented in [1] is the easiest and most straightforward.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the brushless doubly-fed machine can be accurately modeled using a reduced circuit approach.
we have developed two methods for obtaining equivalent circuit parameter for brushless doubly-fed machine.
the coupled-circuit model is a good tool to predict the machine behavior and the winding factor approach is a good tool for parameter determination.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the reduced coupled-circuit method can be used to obtain equivalent circuit parameters for brushless doubly fed machines.
a single equivalent loop model of the rotor is sufficient to determine the equivalent circuit parameters for a brushless doubly fed motor.
both methods are viable and provide a good starting point for the design of a brushless doubly fed motor.
